newsitem.title: JAPAN: German banker warns of EMU-related capital flight.
newsitem.headline: German banker warns of EMU-related capital flight.

text.p: A senior German banker on Tuesday warned about flight of capital if nations were to rush ahead and launch Europe's currency union on time even though nations are not yet fully ready to permanently link their currencies.

"I personally consider it a risk if monetary union were to be commenced without fundamental reform of economic policy being irrevocably launched in the countries seeking membership (in Europe's currency union)," said Gerd Haeusler, a member of the management board at Dresdner Bank AG.
"It would be risky to give priority to the timetable for monetary union over the fulfilment of the criteria," he added.
Europe's currency union is scheduled to begin on January 1, 1999 with as many nations who meet the rigorous entry criteria.
Haeusler was participating in Global 24, a conference on monetary union from Tokyo and a text of his speech was made available in Frankfurt.

Haeusler stressed that currencies thrive through the confidence investors place in them. Consequently "any attempt to squeeze countries with a stability deficit into monetary union against our better knowledge is bound to weaken its standing," Haeusler warned.

Haeusler warned that international investors would know how to take "evasive action". And in light of public reservations about the project outside of Europe and particulary in Asia, "it is vital to abide by the commitments that have been made," Haeusler said.
